title: Lower bound on $1 - e^{-\eta}$
statement:
For every real number $\eta > 0$, the quantity $1 - e^{-\eta}$ is bounded below by its second-order Taylor expansion at the origin:
\[
  1 - e^{-\eta} \;\ge\; \eta - \frac{\eta^{2}}{2}.
\]
replaced:
For $\eta > 0$,
\[
  1 - e^{-\eta} \;\ge\; \eta - \frac{\eta^2}{2}.
\]
This follows directly from the quadratic bound $e^{-\eta} \le 1 - \eta + \eta^2/2$.
